messages:
maya-dev: Heads up — ~18% of GPU nodes in us-west2 are reporting NotReady + NoSchedule. Kubelet shows device plugin failing to open the socket.

sam-infra: pinging infra oncall. any recent nodepool or kernel rollouts?

leo-sre: Not seeing cluster-wide kernel bumps in the deploy log. I can grab kubelet + device-plugin logs from one affected node.

maya-dev: paste from one node: ```May 3 09:11:23 gpu-node-43 kubelet[1234]: E0503 09:11:23.456 kubelet.go:234] device-plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create device plugin endpoint: open /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: permission denied```

ashley-eng: interesting — that path is a hostPath mounted by the DS. Could be selinux or perms after a subpath mount change. Any recent changes to the DS securityContext?

sam-infra: I didn't touch it. infra-bot shows a rolling restart of the nvidia-driver-daemonset earlier for a driver hotpatch (infra/driver-update-2026-05-03) — maybe the restart changed owner on /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins.

leo-sre: can we check file perms on node? `ssh gpu-node-43 sudo ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins`

maya-dev: output: ``drwxr-x--- 2 root root 4096 May 3 09:10 .`` and `srw-rw---- 1 root root 0 May 3 09:10 nvidia.sock`

ashley-eng: the DS expects the socket to be writable by plugin account. current nvidia-device-plugin runs as non-root? it's set to runAsUser: 65534 in our manifest AFAIK. if owner is root:root and perms 660, then non-root can't open it.

sam-infra: yep, device-plugin container runs as nobody. quick fix is to restart the DS as root so it recreates socket with correct perms, or change hostPath mount options/perms. I'm going to `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin` and watch nodes.

leo-sre: also cluster-autoscaler is failing to scale up GPU pool because nodes stay tainted NoSchedule. we should temporarily adjust pod tolerations for critical jobs or scale dedicated CPU nodes to handle backlog. Cost hit but necessary.

sam-infra: restarted DS. logs show plugin now failing with same permission denied on some nodes but success on others. pattern: failed nodes were the ones that got the driver hotpatch earlier.

maya-dev: any chance the driver install script changed `umask` or created the socket before the kubelet chowns the dir?

ashley-eng: driver installer writes to `/var/lib/nvidia` during install. If the installer runs as root and creates files with 700 perms, then plugin cannot bind. We should update the installer to set `chmod 755` on device-plugins dir and `chmod 660` on the socket with group `kube` or run plugin as root until we patch.

leo-sre: short-term mitigation plan: 1) taint affected nodes `NoSchedule` already present; 2) cordon + drain noncritical pods from affected nodes; 3) run a daemonset job that fixes perms: `kubectl -n kube-system run fix-nvidia-perms --restart=OnFailure --image=alpine --command -- sh -c \"chmod 755 /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins || true; chown root:root /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins || true\"` -> target using nodeSelector for gpu nodes.

sam-infra: created a job to fix perms on all affected nodes (rolling). Patching driver installperms ticket: INFRA-2109.

maya-dev: after perms fix, nodes transition to Ready and device-plugin registers. Monitoring token: infra-bot shows 12 nodes recovered, 6 still failing (manual intervention required).

ashley-eng: I'll open an MR to make nvidia-device-plugin run as root temporarily (with note) and update the installer to explicitly set socket perms. longer term we should change the plugin to support dropping privileges after bind.

leo-sre: cluster-autoscaler backlog: ramped CPU-only cluster by +20% to absorb queued jobs. cost estimate for 24h ~ +$3.2k if we keep that up. flagging for finance.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-133 — "nvidia device plugin socket perms after driver hotpatch -> GPU nodes NotReady". P1.

sam-infra: documenting recovery steps in the incident doc. tagging @ashley-eng @leo-sre for follow-ups on MR. :thumbsup:

maya-dev: thanks. keep me posted if any nodes re-fail. I'll throttle driver hotpatch rollout until we have a fix.

deploy-bot: FYI: scheduled driver hotpatch rollout paused for us-west2 until INFRA-2109 resolves.
